purpose: Stable contract for humans, code and future AI agents. Views project canonical objects; they never own or replace domain data.
update_rules: Preserve stable ids across UI redesigns.
Never replace an entire domain collection because one view changed.
Merge imported objects by stable source id; do not duplicate them.
Unknown fields must survive read-modify-write cycles.
Renderers may branch on type/capability, never on personal names such as a student or expense label.

Raw behavior storage may omit a day. Projection semantics depend on tracker mode: negative-event trackers treat absence of an explicit negative mark after activation as baseline/clear, while positive-extra trackers treat absence as neutral/unmarked.
Calendar, Habits and Money are projections over shared objects, not separate data silos.
Migrations must be additive and versioned; destructive changes require an explicit migration.
UI-only changes must not mutate canonical data.
Before publishing, verify that baseline calendar objects still render and that saved local state remains readable.

calendar_week: The week is seven days and the current product view starts on Sunday.
Visible 30-minute empty slots are interactive; compressed time is not.
A whole-week internal empty span may be compressed only when it is at least 90 minutes.
A compressed span is exactly one full-width passive band using the secondary theme color.
The only text inside a compressed span is TIEMPO LIBRE in the primary theme color.
Compressed spans never show duration, arrows, day dividers, buttons, focus states or manual expansion.
No dynamic content may become unreachable because of overflow clipping or a hard-coded embedded height.
A surface has one vertical scroll owner.
habit_history: The visible history uses exactly fourteen equal day columns ending at HOY on the far right.
Every tracker row has one fixed height independent of label length, streak state or recorded values.

The primary tracker row contains only the tracker name, its fourteen day marks and the graph chevron. Permanent streak counts, badges, metrics, explanatory text and extra controls are forbidden there.
A small chevron at the right edge of the tracker label is an actual control and may toggle only that tracker's graph.
Repeated taps on a day cell cycle directly through only that tracker's meaningful states and finally back to blank; no editor strip, menu or expanding button row appears.
A two-stroke geometric X has one universal meaning: an undesired event. It must never represent a positive completion.
A solid filled day block has one universal meaning: an explicitly recorded positive event or completion.
A small inner dot is reserved for an intermediate warning state such as craving in an addiction tracker.
Blank has no drawn symbol. On negative-event trackers it is the automatic baseline/no-negative-event state after activation; on positive Extras it means no positive event was explicitly recorded.
Graph toggles do not alter tracker-row height; an opened graph is inserted as its own row immediately below the tracker and above the next tracker.
The left-side cell created beneath a tracker when its graph is open is the designated secondary-information rail.
Current streak and best previous streak may appear only inside that secondary-information rail, never beside the tracker name.
Automatic daily streaks belong to negative-event trackers; positive Extras are not penalized for unmarked days and do not show daily streak stats by default.
Current streak is represented by an enlarged monochrome flame plus its number, without a repeated RACHA label.
Best previous streak is represented by a monochrome trophy plus its number and the date on which that streak ended, without a repeated MEJOR label; omit the trophy row when no previous streak exists.
Streak information is never a pill, chip, button or colored badge.
Each tracker graph can be opened or closed independently and the visibility choice is a view preference, not behavior data.
Habit categories are explicit full-width title bands rather than anonymous spacer rows or divider lines.
Each category title band is itself a toggle that may collapse or reveal all trackers in that category.
Collapsing a category changes only presentation; it never changes behavior logs or each tracker's remembered graph-open preference.
Category titles contain only the category name and a minimal chevron; do not add counts, badges, summaries or KPI text there.
Daily marks and trajectory points share the exact same fourteen X centers.
habit_trajectory: Each tracker owns one separate spacious solid line; tracker lines are never overlaid in one chart.
A trajectory is normally hidden until its own row toggle is opened.
An opened trajectory is visually attached to its tracker row instead of living in a detached dashboard section.
All trajectory lines use the same active theme color and are identified by the tracker immediately above them, not by dashed patterns or a legend.
The HOY divider is a temporal boundary in the date axis and day-cell register only; it must never run vertically through an opened trajectory plot.
For Adicciones and Rutina negative-event trackers, the minimum baseline means no recent negative disturbance; an X creates a strong upward spike and a craving dot creates a smaller one.
For negative-event trackers, unmarked days decay the residual disturbance toward zero automatically; the user is not required to mark a good day.
For positive Extras, an explicit filled completion creates recent positive activity and unmarked days decay that activity without counting as failure.
Nearby events accumulate instead of resetting to an identical isolated shape.
Trajectory is derived from behavior logs and is never persisted as a second source of truth.
Do not show numeric scores, chart legends, line-style keys, KPI chips or explanatory badges in the default trajectory view.
money_surface: The primary financial question is how much projected money remains in the selected month.
The default Money surface is monthly and temporal; do not restore a six-month dual-line dashboard as the primary view.
QUEDA PROYECTADO is visually primary; ENTRA and SALE are secondary readouts, not cards.
The next important dated movements are shown as a simple chronological flow below the monthly balance.
Lesson income is derived from canonical calendar classes and must not be duplicated as manually maintained finance records.
Potential income is visually secondary and never added to confirmed projected remaining money.
Expenses, obligations and recurring payments preserve their own status and date rather than collapsing into one monthly number.
Income, expenses, recurring items and history live in collapsed disclosure rows until the user asks for detail.
Financial data is expressed with typography, position, weight and geometry; only actual actions receive button affordance.
The Money surface uses only the active two-color theme, including dark palettes.
Mobile reorganizes the temporal flow vertically rather than shrinking a desktop chart.
Legacy finance v1 values are migrated additively and remain readable.
Personal financial amounts must not be hard-coded into the public repository; a private URL-fragment seed may write them to localStorage and must remove the fragment immediately after import.

legacy_behavior_visibility.news: Noticias is removed from the default UI but its historical state must be preserved if present.

habit_mark_model.blank_negative_tracker: automatic baseline/no negative event after tracker activation

habit_trajectory_model.meaning: recent tracker activity: residual negative disturbance for negative-event trackers and recent positive activity for Extras
habit_trajectory_model.rule: Changing the derived trajectory model must never rewrite historical logs.

finance_projection_model.primary_formula: confirmed scheduled income minus confirmed expenses and active recurring expenses
finance_projection_model.potential_income_rule: shown separately and excluded from QUEDA PROYECTADO
finance_projection_model.calendar_income_rule: derive lesson occurrences from canonical calendar classes using duration × rate
finance_projection_model.privacy_rule: public code defines behavior and schema; personal amounts remain in browser-local state

whatsapp_export.rule: Never commit inferred dates or times without review when confidence is low.

google_calendar.output: canonical events with external source ids
google_calendar.rule: External ids are retained so future syncs update instead of duplicate.
